paragraphs.notes: The whole page body is one Markush enumeration table with no prose at all, so zh and en are the same string: every cell is a chemical symbol or an abbreviation, and there is no German to translate. The zh field holds the verbatim transcription, since this is a German-language WO publication and not Chinese. The document carries no [00NN] paragraph markers; marker is the compound-number range as printed. The page carries no Tabelle caption and no drawn scaffold: the caption fixing the shared substituents and the header row's meaning sit on an earlier page, so the table continues here mid-run beginning at Nr. 71. The header row is printed as Nr., R with superscript 7a, R with superscript 7b, R with superscript 12, L, R with superscript 1; superscripts are flattened in the transcription. Every SO2 and CH2 is printed with a subscript 2, flattened here. Rows 73 and 97 have their R12 cell indented by roughly one character relative to the other rows; the text is the same PhSO2 and the indent is typesetting, not content. A small ink speck sits directly above the O of O-c-Pentyl in the R1 cell of row 72; it is scan noise, not a diacritic or a prime. A short horizontal tick follows O-c-Bu in the R1 cell of row 90, level with the baseline; it is scan noise and not a hyphen, since the cell ends there and no continuation follows. Bz is the printed abbreviation and is transcribed as printed rather than expanded. Nothing follows row 97: the lower quarter of the page is blank, and the table is cut off mid-run to continue on the next page.
